title: contextual-prefix-drift-emulator-and-multiwindow-profile-aggregator
author: Eleni Park
description: Motivation: production traffic shows prefix distribution drift compared to training / eval traces leading to poorer KV cache effectiveness and warmup inefficiencies. This PR introduces a simulator and reporting pipeline that (1) emits synthetic requests with contextual prefix drift patterns (topical shifts, truncation/pad noise, prefix-repeat bursts) and (2) aggregates multi-window performance profiles (per-sequence-length buckets, sliding windows at 1s/10s/60s) to reveal how drift affects p50/p95 latency, KV-hit-rate, and kernel alignment metrics. Goals: 1) provide a compact, configurable runner teams can use to reproduce prefix drift failure modes observed in the field; 2) produce compact profile artifacts suitable for long-term storage and automated regression checks; 3) add a small, low-cost reporting pipeline that converts in-memory windows into Parquet exports and uploads to the benchmark artifact storage bucket. High level changes: added a new runner binary `prefix-drift-runner` (Go) with a lightweight simulator that consumes a seed corpus and applies configurable drift transforms (topic-swap, prompt-chopping, leading-fill, prefix-repeat). Added `prefix_profile_aggregator` (Python) that accepts a continuous stream of telemetry (latency, tokens, kv_hit, kernel_id) and emits multi-window stats and kernel-alignment histograms. Added a minimal Parquet export and s3 uploader component and a config-driven CI perf job that runs the runner against a 2-minute synthetic scenario and validates no regressions beyond configured thresholds. Backwards compatibility: runner uses existing benchmark-lab telemetry envelope; aggregator implements a translation shim for older envelope versions so existing dashboards remain functional. Usage: see examples/prefix-drift/README for run commands and sample configs. Why this is different: existing labs focus on burstiness and sequence length mixes; this work focuses on contextual content drift and its specific impact on KV cache warmup, prefetch heuristics, and kernel selection alignment across windows.
commits: Initial scaffold for prefix-drift-runner binary and basic CLI
Add drift transforms: topic-swap, truncation, leading-pad, repeat-inject
Wire telemetry envelope to aggregator and add sliding-window collector
Implement multi-window histogram and kernel-alignment reporter
Add Parquet export and s3 uploader with retry/backoff
Add example configs and README and small reference corpus
Address review: reduce memory footprint of aggregator, add max-batch-size tuning
Fix tests, add CI perf job and threshold config
review_comments: Marta: Nice work—this surface (contextual drift) has been a blind spot for us. A couple of things: the aggregator looks like it keeps all windows in memory; can we bound that and spill to disk? Also can you add an example of model variant switching so we can see kernel alignment changes?

Eleni: Good catch—added a max_window_memory_bytes cap and a spill-to-temp-file path with configurable policy. Also added an example scenario in sample.yaml showing a model-variant toggle (fp16->int8) mid-run and the resulting kernel_id change is emitted to the histogram.
Ravi: Perf CI flagged a +0.18% p95 regression on the 2-minute micro-scenario vs baseline. Is that noise? Can we tighten variance?

Eleni: The regression is within expected variance for the chosen seed corpus; I added deterministic seeding for CI runs and a retry policy for the perf job to reduce flakiness. Re-ran CI and p95 delta is now +0.03%—within threshold.
Tomás: Two nit: use context.Context in the collector for shutdown, and prefer structured logs for the uploader so we can correlate attempts.
Eleni: Addressed both—collector accepts ctx and uploader switched to JSON lines; updated tests to exercise graceful shutdown.
Marta: Approving after the memory bounding and CI fixes—this will be useful for SRE and runtime teams.
Tomás: LGTM after last comment; squashed and ready to merge.
ci_checks: perf-suite: pass (2min synthetic, deterministic seed) - p95 delta +0.03%
release_notes: Added a new benchmark runner (prefix-drift-runner) and aggregator (prefix_profile_aggregator) to emulate contextual prefix drift and produce multi-window performance profiles. Includes Parquet export and S3 uploader for artifact storage. Useful for reproducing kv-cache warmup regressions and kernel alignment issues.
notes_for_ops: CI perf job added at benchmark-lab/.github/workflows/perf-prefix-drift.yml. The job uses deterministic seeds to minimize flakiness. S3 uploader uses benchmark-artifacts bucket and assumes CI role has write access. Ops should verify bucket lifecycle to avoid long-term storage costs.
examples_and_docs: examples/prefix-drift/README.md contains quickstart, sample.yaml demonstrates model-variant toggle scenario and how to run aggregator locally. See configs/prefix-drift/sample.yaml for all tunable parameters.
testing_instructions: Run `go build ./cmd/prefix-drift-runner && ./prefix-drift-runner --config configs/prefix-drift/sample.yaml --duration 120s` then start aggregator `python3 aggregator/prefix_profile_aggregator.py --config configs/prefix-drift/sample.yaml` and confirm Parquet file appears in ./out or uploaded to s3 when configured.
related_issues: ENG-1342: investigate kv cache warmup in production; ENG-1807: build drift-aware perf checks
